problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y(3\sqrt{x}+2),\,y(0)=2
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y(1),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y(1)≈{{field-1}}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=y({x}^{2}+1),\,y(-1)=\frac{11}{3}
$$

Use the trapezoidal method with one step to approximate $y\,(-\frac{1}{2}),$ rounded to two decimal places.

$$
y\,(-\frac{1}{2})≈{{field-1}}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the trapezoidal method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
Δy=\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx,
$$

with ${y}_{\text{new}}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{\text{new}})$ evaluated at the next $x$ and $y$ values.

First, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=-\frac{1}{2}-(-1)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, let's proceed with the trapezoidal method. In general, $Δy$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{2}({y}^{′}+{y}_{\text{new}}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(y({x}^{2}+1)+{y}_{\text{new}}(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1))\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute this into ${y}_{\text{new}}=y+Δy:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+1)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+1) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+5)+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}+\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve for the general formula for ${y}_{\text{new}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}-\frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}({x}_{\text{new}})^{2} & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+5) \\ \frac{1}{4}{y}_{\text{new}}(3-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}) & =\frac{1}{4}y({x}^{2}+5) \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y({x}^{2}+5)}{3-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, in the first step, the new $x$ value is ${x}_{\text{new}}=-1+\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}.$ Hence, the new $y$ value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =\frac{y({x}^{2}+5)}{3-({x}_{\text{new}})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{11}{3}((-1)^{2}+5)}{3-{(-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{22}{(\frac{11}{4})} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $y\,(-\frac{1}{2})≈8.00.$
